title: App Registrations and Service Principals
description: Learn how to register an application in Entra ID and understand the difference between an app registration and a service principal.

data.text: An app registration is a blueprint — it defines your app's identity, redirect URIs, and the permissions it needs. A service principal is the local identity your app uses at runtime in a specific tenant.

cards.title: App Registration
cards.description: The global definition of your application in Entra ID.

cards.title: Service Principal
cards.description: The security principal used by your app in one tenant.

data.title: Create an App Registration with Azure CLI
data.content: Register a new application in Entra ID using the Azure CLI. This creates the app registration.

data.title: Create a Service Principal with Azure CLI
data.content: After registering the app, create a service principal so the app can sign in and get tokens.

data.title: Practice: Register a Demo App
data.description: In the Azure Portal, navigate to Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Name it 'demo-api', set redirect URI to 'https://jwt.ms', and save the Application (client) ID.
steps: Open Azure Portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
Click Register and copy the Application (client) ID.
data.expectedOutcome: You will have a new app registration and be able to see its client ID in the overview pane.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: An app registration defines what your app is.
A service principal is what your app uses in a tenant to authenticate.
One app registration can have many service principals across tenants.
